Likelihood and prior

Source: vignettes/articles/methods-objective.Rmd
methods-objective.Rmd

Without a prior, dMod2 estimates by maximum likelihood and minimizes \(-2 \log L\). With a prior, it minimizes \(-2 \log\) of the posterior up to a constant, and the minimum is the maximum a posteriori estimate [1]. Guide: Setting up models; derivatives: Sensitivities and Hessians.

Data term

normL2() computes twice the negative log-likelihood of independent Gaussian errors, for data \(y_j\), predictions \(f_j(\theta)\) and standard deviations \(\sigma_j(\theta)\):

\[-2 \log L(\theta) = \sum_j \left( \frac{(y_j - f_j(\theta))^2}{\sigma_j(\theta)^2} + \log \sigma_j(\theta)^2 \right) + \text{const}. \tag{1}\]

\(\log \sigma_j^2\) is constant for given \(\sigma_j\) and bounds an estimated \(\sigma_j\): the first term of (1) falls as \(\sigma_j\) grows, the second rises.

Error model

\(\sigma_j\) comes from the data column sigma where set, otherwise from the error model, an obsfn \(\sigma = e(f, \theta)\) of prediction and parameters. A constant \(\sigma\) on a log-scale observable \(y = \log(s\, x + o)\) is a relative error: to first order, \(\sigma\) in \(\log z\) is \(\sigma z\) in \(z\).

Prior

constraintL2() adds a Gaussian prior with means \(\mu_k\) and standard deviations \(s_k\),

\[-2 \log \pi(\theta) = \sum_k \left( \frac{\theta_k - \mu_k}{s_k} \right)^2, \tag{2}\]

added to the data term by +. On the log scale, a prior far wider than the data leaves determined parameters in place and keeps undetermined ones finite, so the minimum exists without bounds. The Hessian of (2) is \(2/s_k^2\) on the diagonal.

Further terms

  • constraintStability(): keeps the steady state of a Pimpl() stable (Steady states).
  • datapointL2(): a data point whose value is a parameter, for validation profiles [2].

Each term is an objfn; a sum keeps the parts as attributes, so profiles and likelihood ratios read the data term alone.

Reference: normL2(), constraintL2(), datapointL2(), constraintStability(), Y()

References

[1]
D. Kaschek, W. Mader, M. Fehling-Kaschek, M. Rosenblatt, and J. Timmer, “dMod: Efficient parameter estimation and uncertainty analysis for dynamic models,” Journal of Statistical Software, vol. 88, no. 10, pp. 1–32, 2019, doi: 10.18637/jss.v088.i10.
[2]
C. Kreutz, A. Raue, and J. Timmer, “Likelihood based observability analysis and confidence intervals for predictions of dynamic models,” BMC Systems Biology, vol. 6, p. 120, 2012, doi: 10.1186/1752-0509-6-120.
